name: v3
_comment: Policy v3 (depth-aware): the delegation policy validated by the paid A/B
evaluation described in docs/DELEGATION-ROUTING.md. JSON, not YAML, because
this package has no runtime dependencies (pyproject.toml) and this file is
read on a delegation's critical path.
Result it reproduces: standard depth -62% cost per sufficient task (n=8),
thorough -63% (n=13); ~22% of delegations moved. It FAILED its pre-registered
preference measure -- see the doc's Evidence section before trusting it.
_comment_tiers: Tier of a resolved model, by name pattern, first match wins.
_comment_context: Estimated input tokens = floor + chars/chars_per_token; a candidate is
skipped when that exceeds its window budget.
_comment_base_threshold: Below this probability the tier answer is not acted on at all.

_comment: Effort-down on a small-tier anchor was measured unsafe (sample s134,
haiku anchor: arm A acceptable, arm B not).

_comment_effort_target: The effort lever keeps the anchor's own provider and model and only lowers
reasoning effort. No context_window: the model is unchanged, so the
_comment_moves: Candidate ladders, ordered: the first candidate that fits the context
window and meets the predicted capability requirements is chosen.
_comment_depth: Depth x base move -> what to do.

brief.reason: brief depth was never observed or measured (0 of 200 sampled delegations)

keep.reason: thorough depth with no tier signal - no safe move

_comment_requirements: Predicted requirement -> capability a candidate must have.
_comment_capabilities: Capability facts, matched against a candidate model name by substring.
ONLY verified facts belong here; an absent model or capability is UNKNOWN,
and unknown is allowed (never silently blocks a candidate).
claude-sonnet-5-5: verified to reject the computer-use tool type
computer_20251124, so it can never be picked for a computer-use delegation.
